title: How nuclear power stations work
examples: How is the heat created in a nuclear power station?
What is the job of the control rods?
Does the steam go directly to the electricity?

explain.say: Today we learn how nuclear power stations make electricity.
First, we look at nuclear fission. Fission is splitting a large atom's nucleus.

items: Neutron: The particle that hits it

explain.say: When fission happens, it releases a lot of heat and more neutrons.
This heat is used to boil water, which creates high-pressure steam.

draw.text: Heat creates steam to turn turbine.

explain.say: The steam then pushes against the blades of a steam turbine, making it spin very fast.
Finally, the spinning turbine connects to a generator to produce usable electricity.

faq.q: What is the difference between fission and fusion?
faq.a: Fission is splitting a large atom, like uranium. Fusion is joining two small atoms together, like in the sun.
asks: Is fission the same as joining atoms?
What is the opposite of splitting atoms?

faq.q: Why do we need control rods in the reactor?
faq.a: Control rods absorb excess neutrons to keep the fission reaction at a steady rate. This prevents the reaction from getting too fast.
asks: What do the control rods manage?
How do we slow down the reaction?

faq.q: Is the steam dangerous to touch?
faq.a: The steam is under very high pressure and temperature. It must be handled by specialized equipment.
asks: What pressure is the steam under?

faq.q: Does the electricity go straight from the reactor?
faq.a: No, the heat makes steam, which spins the turbine, and the turbine powers a generator to make electricity.
asks: What is the path from heat to power?

faq.q: What material is used as fuel in these stations?
faq.a: The main fuel material used is Uranium-235. This is the source material for the fission process.
asks: What atom is split for power?
Where does the fuel come from?

facts: Fission is the process of splitting a heavy atomic nucleus.
This splitting releases significant amounts of heat energy.
The heat boils water to create high-pressure steam.
Control rods absorb excess neutrons to manage the reaction rate.

quiz.say: The spinning turbine is connected to which device to make power?
quiz.why: The generator uses the mechanical energy of the spinning turbine to create electricity.

wrong.0: Steam is the force that spins the turbine, but it is not the device that makes electricity.
wrong.1: The boiler's job is to create the steam, not to convert motion into electricity.
wrong.3: Control rods manage the reaction rate, they do not generate electricity.

quiz.say: If the fission reaction speeds up too much, what component must be used to slow it down?
quiz.why: Control rods absorb extra neutrons, which slows down the fission reaction safely.

wrong.1: Adding more steam would increase pressure, making the reaction faster, not slower.
wrong.2: The generator only converts motion to electricity; it does not control the atomic reaction.
wrong.3: While coolant is used, the specific tool for controlling the rate of fission is the control rod.
